paper_metadata.title: Effect of Cr and Ni/Fe Ratio on the Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of γ'-Strengthened Ni-Fe-Based Alloys

evidence.quote: To continue to meet the future materials’ requirements for advanced power generation systems, enhancing the mechanical properties and long-term phase stability of Ni–Fe-based alloys is needed.
In summary, the composition of 25Cr35Ni austenitic stainless steel was modiﬁed to create a series of experimental alloys

Four experimental Ni–Fe-based alloys were fabricated with diﬀerent Ni/Fe and Cr concentrations by alloying the original 25Cr35Ni alloy with high-purity Ni, Fe, Al, and Ti-alloying additions in an MRF ABJ-900 (MRF Inc., Suncook, NH) arc melter under a gettered Ar atmosphere.

the ingots were melted, ﬂipped, and remelted a minimum of ﬁve times.
Samples designated A1, A2, A3, and A4 were homogenized at 1200 °C for 40 hours, following with air cooling to ambient temperature.

After soaking at 1050 °C for 1 hour, the specimens were subjected to a multi-pass hot-rolling process to reﬁne the coarse-grained, homogenized microstructure. During hot rolling, the thickness of the ingots had a total reduction of approximately 70 pct, and no strain-induced cracking was observed.

After hot rolling, the specimens were heat treated at 1000 °C for 2 hours to enable complete recrystallization of the microstructure and form an equiaxed grain structure prior to being air cooled to room temperature.
The rolled specimens were then aged at 750 °C for 20 hours before air cooling to ambient temperature.
The long-term-exposed specimens were then heat treated at 750 °C for 200 hours (Table II).
